summary: Kashi Prasad Jayaswal was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at the University of Allahabad, Jesus College, and the University of Oxford (M.A., ~1906–1909), and was a Lecturer in Ancient Indian History at the University of Calcutta in 1910.

Kashinath Narayan Dikshit was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. Succeeding Rakhaldas Bandyopadhyay, he served as Director General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India in 1937.

Kashinath Trimbak Telang was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Mumbai and Elphinstone College (~1864–1868), where he later served as Senior Dakshina Fellow (~1867–1872).

Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat College (~1913–1945) and Hon. Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1945–1957).

Kate Crosby is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. She earned her PhD from Oxford under committee member Lance S. Cousins (~1994–1999) and held posts at Cardiff University, the Buddhist Institute, and SOAS University of London (~2002–2013).
Kate Wharton is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. from SOAS University of London (~2003–2008) and held a post at Birkbeck, University of London.
Katharina Sabernig is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the University of Vienna in 2017 and held a post at the Medical University of Vienna.
Katherine Anne Narraway works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied at McGill University (~2006–2008), where she earned a Master of Arts supervised by G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Katherine Anne Paul works in Tibetology, history/archaeology, and Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Gudrun Bühnemann, along with teachers Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam V. Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.

Katherine Janiec Jones works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied at Davidson College (~1991–1995) and completed her PhD at the University of Chicago (~1995–2002) under doctoral supervisor Paul J. Griffiths.

Katherine K. Young is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Chicago (~1968–1972) and McGill University (~1972–1978), where she later served as Professor (~1978–2014).

Kathleen D. Morrison is a history/archaeology and Indology scholar. She studied at Notre Dame, New Mexico, and UC Berkeley (~1987–1992), and held posts at Northwestern University (~1994–1995) and the University of Pennsylvania (~2017).

Kathleen M. Erndl was an Indology and religious studies scholar. She held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, DePauw University, Lewis & Clark College (~1989–1993), and Florida State University (~1993–2017).

Kathleen McDonald is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers including Tenzin Gyatso, 14th Dalai Lama, Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Ngawang Dhargyey, Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche.
Kathrin Holz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and held a research affiliation at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Kathryn H. Selig Brown is a scholar of Tibetology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Michigan (~1994–2000) under doctoral supervisor Walter M. Spink.

Katia Buffetrille is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She studied under Alexander W. Macdonald, completed a PhD at Paris Nanterre University (~1990–1996), and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2001).

Katsuhiko Kamimura was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1964–1973) and under Minoru Hara and V. Raghavan. He held academic posts at Kokugakuin University (~1976–1983) and the University of Tokyo (~1983–2003).
Katsuhiro Yoshizawa is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar. He studied at Doshisha University (~1964–1968) and served as Professor at Hanazono University (~1993–2016).

Katsumi Mimaki is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Kyoto University, INALCO, and Paris/Sorbonne Nouvelle (PhD, ~1972–1977), and later served as Professor at Kyoto University (~1977–2011).
